rows.text: A particle of mass \(m\) is rotating in a circular orbit of radius \(r\) under the action of gravity in the presence of another stationary particle of very large mass \(M\) (\(M \gg m\)). Consider that the gravitational potential energy is zero at infinite separation. If the total energy of the rotating particle is \(E\), then, which of the following expressions correctly represents the angular momentum of the particle?

A point electric charge \(Q\) is placed at a corner of a cube as shown in the figure. What is the electric flux passing through the shaded surface ABCD of the cube? (\(\epsilon_\circ\) is permittivity of free space)

figure.note: A cube drawn in perspective with its top face ABCD shaded (A and B the back top corners, D and C the front top corners). The charge Q (a dot) sits at the bottom corner directly below D.

rows.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
rows.text: Neutral gas molecules, each of mass \(m\), are at a temperature \(T\) in a container at zero gravity. How does the average de Broglie wavelength \(\lambda\) of a molecule depend on \(T\)?

rows.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
rows.text: Consider a particle of unit mass being thrown with an initial velocity \(v_\circ\) making an angle \(\phi\) with the horizontal ground. What is the magnitude of the angular momentum of the particle about the point of projection at a time \(t\) after its projection while it is in flight?
Consider two long thin conductors \(A\) and \(B\) each carrying current \(I\) as shown in the figure. Considering \(A\) to be fixed, which of the following statements is correct?

figure.note: Axes x (to the right), y (up) and z (out of the page, drawn slanting down-left) from an origin. Conductor B lies along the y-axis above the origin carrying current I upward (+y). Conductor A is a horizontal wire parallel to the x-axis, below the origin, crossing the z-axis line, carrying current I towards +x; a dotted vertical line drops from the origin down to A's level.

options: \(B\) experiences a net force along \(+x\) axis.
\(B\) experiences a net force along \(-x\) axis.

rows.subtopic: Kinetic Theory of an Ideal Gas
rows.text: What is the average kinetic energy of molecules of an ideal gas leaking freely through an orifice of a container which has \(N\) molecules at pressure \(P\) in volume \(V\)?
Which of the following is an expression for energy in terms of the Planck's constant \(h\), the velocity of light \(c\) and the Gravitational constant \(G\)?

A solid block on a frictionless surface is connected to two rigid supports on the left and right side by springs of spring constants \(k\) and \(4k\) respectively as shown in the figure. The time spent by the block in a complete cycle of oscillation on the left and the right side of the equilibrium position are \(t_L\) and \(t_R\), respectively. Which of the following is correct?

figure.note: A block on a horizontal surface between two vertical walls; a spring of constant k joins the left wall to the block and a spring of constant 4k joins the block to the right wall.

rows.text: A capacitor with capacitance \(C_\circ\) consists of two concentric spherical conductors. If the radii of the inner and the outer spherical conductors are halved, what is the new capacitance?
What is the time \(t\) taken by the capacitor in the given circuit to charge to \(1/\sqrt{2\pi}\) of its full capacity?

figure.note: A diamond-shaped circuit with top, left, right and bottom corners. Top-left side: resistor R. Top-right side: cell V. Bottom-left side: cell V. Bottom-right side: resistor R. A capacitor C joins the top corner to the bottom corner.

rows.subtopic: Line Spectra of the Hydrogen Atom
rows.text: The allowed energy levels of electrons in a Hydrogen atom are given by \(E_n = -13.6/n^2\) eV. For electronic transition in Hydrogen atom, what is the maximum frequency of the emitted photon? (\(h = 6.62 \times 10^{-34}\) Js; e = \(1.6 \times 10^{-19}\) C)
Which of the following statements about the P-V diagram of an ideal gas of fixed number of particles is incorrect?
options: Two distinct adiabats never cross each other.
Two distinct isotherms never cross each other.
An isotherm and an adiabat intersect at one point.
An isotherm and an adiabat intersect at more than one point.

rows.text: A cube, a cylinder (of height equal to its diameter) and a sphere, all solid, are made of a metal and are of identical mass. If all the three shapes having initial temperature \(50^\circ C\) are put in a large reservoir of water at \(10^\circ C\). Which of the above three shapes cools the fastest?
options: All three at the same rate.

rows.text: An LED display consists of 100 pixels per \(\mathrm{cm^2}\). Consider that the diameter of the pupil of the eye is 5 mm and the average wavelength of the display is 575 nm. What is the nearest distance from the display one can be at, such that the display does not appear pixelated?

Two equal positive charges (\(q\)) are placed at the vertices \(B\) and \(C\) of an isosceles triangle of base \(a\) and height \(h = 3\sqrt{3}a/2\), as shown in the adjacent figure. When a charge \(q'\) is placed at \(A\), it is found that at a point inside the triangle, the net electric field due to the three charges vanishes. If this point is at a height \(h/3\), then what is \(q'\)?

figure.note: Isosceles triangle with apex A at the top and base BC at the bottom (dots at A, B, C). Base length a marked under BC; height h marked by an arrow on the left from base level to A's level; a dotted horizontal line across the triangle at height h/3 above the base, marked h/3 on the right.
